newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Mediterranean bankers to hold first forum in Tunis.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean bankers to hold first forum in Tunis.

text.p: More than 200 bankers and financial experts are expected to participate in a conference in Tunis on Thursday to discuss financing investment and trade in the Mediterranean countries, officials said on Wednesday.
The two-day "First Europ-Mediterranean Banking Forum" is organised by the Club Financier Mediterraneen (CFM) with the support of the European Commission.

CMF's President Pierre Habib-Deloncle, who is also chairman of France's Societe Marseillaise de Credit, told journalists that the forum will focus on discussing investment risks in an attempt to boost investments in the southern Mediterranean countries.

He said he expects the forum to help establish a permanent network between the region's banks and to identify measures to harmonise and secure financial business as part of efforts to establish an Euro-Mediterranean free-trade zone.
Speakers will include Tunisian Finance Minister Nouri Zorgati, EU officials, and bankers from Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, France, Spain, and Italy.

CMF was established in 1991 at the initiative of the French government to allow decision makers in banks, insurance companies, stock exchanges and financial firms of all the Mediterranean countries to meet and promote better economic and financial relations in the region.
Habib-Deloncle said CMF was currently preparing a project for the establishment of an Euro-Mediterranean investment guarantee agency and a network of the region's capital risk companies.
CMF has 50 members from 11 Mediterranean countries.
